B. Is this measure already running in Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Standardised lung cancer pathway with booked slots. A lung cancer pathway on the Danish/Swedish/Norwegian model: fixed referral criteria, pre-booked CT, PET-CT, bronchoscopy and MDT slots, a named pathway owner, and published time limits for each step.
effect_summary_en: The Swedish registry study gives a lung cancer pathway lead time of 30–44 days, but only 30 % of patients started treatment within it, and it reports no days saved compared with care before the pathway.
supported_en: Scientific Reports (2023) gives a Swedish lung cancer pathway lead time of 30–44 days, met by 30 % of patients.
not_supported_en: No page read shows how many days a lung cancer pathway saves, so the assumed 14 days (range 5–23) is not shown.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer pathway pages say that after a referral a doctor plans further tests, and that a team of specialists gives a treatment recommendation "if needed". They also say tissue sample analysis usually takes 2–3 weeks. They mention no fixed referral criteria, pre-booked slots or time limit for each step, and no VAKE page about a lung cancer pathway was found. A 2023 Scientific Reports study of Sweden gives a lung cancer lead time of 30–44 days, met by only 30 % of patients, and does not measure days saved.
unanswered_en: HUS's cancer waiting-times page (hus.fi "Syövän hoitoonpääsy") did not load, so any lung cancer time limits HUS publishes there are unchecked; no study reporting days saved by a lung cancer pathway was found.
